rows.counterexample_or_fix: W1 is exact: with radii 2^{-(n+k+2)} each U_n is open dense with lambda(U_n) <= sum_k 2^{-(n+k+1)} = 2^{-n}; G = intersection_n U_n is a dense G_delta and lambda(G) <= 2^{-n} for every n, so lambda(G)=0 and no subset of G has lambda=1. The row summary's '2^{1-n}' is a harmless variant of W1's bound. The failure does not depend on choosing Lebesgue: for any Borel probability mu on [0,1], if mu has an atom x then D\{x} is comeager with mu<1, and if mu is atomless a countable dense set can be covered by mu-small open intervals giving a comeager mu-null set; so the falsifier's 'repair by charging the meager set' remark is loose. Row state correct.

W3 is correct: the irrationals in [0,1] are comeager (complement Q is countable, hence meager) and have empty interior (every nonempty open interval meets Q). An open dense set is nonempty, and every nonempty open subset of [0,1] meets Q, so no open-dense-escape set is contained in the irrationals. No hidden hypothesis.

Verdict is right but the stated reason is false: a closed codimension-1 (0-dimensional) submanifold of R need not be finite, e.g. the integers form a closed discrete embedded 0-dimensional submanifold of R. Fix: if R\Z were contained in the irrationals then Q is contained in Z; Z closed then forces Z=R, contradicting Z != D / codim >= 1. (In the compact [0,1] the 'finite' claim is true, and the row could have used D=[0,1].) The counterexample (irrationals are comeager, every FCC-generic set contains rationals) stands.

W2 is correct: F = [0,1]\G is meager and lambda(F)=1, and F contains no comeager subset, since a comeager C' contained in F would make F comeager, hence [0,1] = F union (D\F) meager, contradicting the Baire property of [0,1]. The suggested 'repair' (full support plus a zero-one law) is not a repair: the covering/atom argument above gives, for every Borel probability mu on [0,1], a comeager set with no mu-full-measure subset.
W3 is correct: the irrationals have Lebesgue measure 1 and empty interior, so they contain no nonempty open set; every open dense set is nonempty. Correct, and no more is needed.

W5 is correct: G = [0,1]\C (middle-thirds Cantor set) has lambda(G)=1. A closed embedded codimension>=1 submanifold of the compact 1-manifold [0,1] is a closed discrete subset of a compact space, hence finite; a finite Z (or finite union) cannot contain the uncountable C, so [0,1]\Z is never contained in G. Row state correct.

Correct and hypothesis-free: an open dense U satisfies U = intersection_n U (constant sequence of open dense sets), so U contains a countable intersection of open dense sets and contains itself, i.e. every ODE-generic set is RC-generic. Baire is needed only for non-vacuity of the residual quantifier, not for the transfer, and the file says exactly this in extra_hypothesis.

W4 is correct: the Smith-Volterra-Cantor set C is closed and nowhere dense with lambda(C)>0, so U=[0,1]\C is open dense with lambda(U)=1-lambda(C)<1, and no subset of U has measure 1. Verdict right (the falsifier's final clause about Gaussian measures is garbled but not load-bearing).

W4 is correct: U=[0,1]\C (fat Cantor) is open dense. An FCC-generic set has the form [0,1]\Z with Z finite (closed discrete in a compact 1-manifold), and [0,1]\Z contained in U would force C contained in Z, impossible since C is uncountable. Row state correct.

The implication is correct: a closed embedded finite-codimension submanifold of codim>=1 has empty interior, hence is nowhere dense, so D\Z is open dense and comeager (it contains itself). Finite unions are fine since a finite intersection of open dense sets is open dense. However the extra_hypothesis/falsifier sub-claim about non-closed immersed Z is false for this target: a finite-codim immersed submanifold (second-countable) is locally a graph over an open set, hence a countable union of compact nowhere-dense pieces, hence meager, so its complement is comeager and the transfer to residual_comeager still holds. Closedness is load-bearing only for the open_dense target (D\Z may fail to be open). Row state correct.

'open' is honest: W6 (D=[0,1], Z={0}, mu=delta_0) gives mu(Z)=1, so D\Z is not full-measure and the transfer fails for that declared measure; for an injective-covariance Gaussian on a separable Banach space every proper closed hyperplane is null (the pushforward by a nonzero functional is a nondegenerate 1-dimensional Gaussian), so the transfer holds there. Since full_measure requires a declared mu, no general answer exists. Note the quoted success case covers only hyperplanes, whereas the transfer needs mu(Z)=0 for all closed finite-codim submanifolds; that stronger statement is true for such Gaussians by a finite-dimensional disintegration/Fubini argument, and the file's 'unresolved' flag on sourcing it is appropriate.

Correct: Z closed with empty interior (implied by codim>=1) makes D\Z open and dense, which is exactly an ODE-generic set contained in itself. The falsifier rightly identifies codim 0 (nonempty interior) as the load-bearing exclusion: e.g. Z a closed ball gives open but non-dense complement. No hidden hypothesis.

witnesses.note: Exact. Intervals of radius 2^{-(n+k+2)} have total length sum_k 2^{-(n+k+1)} = 2^{-n}; each U_n is open and dense (contains Q cap [0,1]); G is a dense G_delta and lambda(G) <= lambda(U_n) <= 2^{-n} for every n, so lambda(G)=0.

Correct. D\G is the complement of a comeager set, hence meager, and lambda(D\G) = 1 - 0 = 1. Its use to refute full_measure->residual_comeager also needs [0,1] to be Baire, which holds; a comeager subset of a meager set would make [0,1] meager.
Correct. Q cap [0,1] is countable, hence meager, so the irrationals are comeager; every nonempty open interval contains a rational, so the interior is empty; Lebesgue measure is 1.

Correct. The Smith-Volterra-Cantor set is closed, nowhere dense (empty interior), with 0 < lambda(C) < 1; U=[0,1]\C is open (closed complement) and dense (C has empty interior), and lambda(U)=1-lambda(C)<1.

Correct as stated for [0,1]: any codim>=1 closed embedded submanifold of the compact 1-manifold [0,1] is a closed discrete subset of a compact space, hence finite, and a finite set cannot contain the uncountable middle-thirds Cantor set, so no FCC-generic set lies in G. Caution: the analogous 'finite' claim would be false in R (the integers are an infinite closed 0-dimensional embedded submanifold); the witness is safe only because it lives in the compact [0,1]. This is exactly the slip that appears in the RC->FCC row's prose.

Correct. Z={0} is a codimension-1 closed embedded submanifold and delta_0(Z)=1, so delta_0(D\Z)=0 and D\Z is not full-measure; hence finite_codimension_complement->full_measure fails for that declared measure. Pedantic note: {0} is a boundary point of the manifold-with-boundary [0,1]; using D=R avoids the quibble. Conclusion unaffected.

most_important_error: No row verdict, definition, witness, or order relation is wrong: all 12 states (8 fails, 3 holds, 1 open), the four definitions, the strength order (FCC > ODE > RC with FM incomparable/conditional), and W1-W6 are mathematically correct. The genuine errors are two false sub-claims in explanatory prose. (a) The row residual_comeager->finite_codimension_complement asserts that every codim>=1 closed submanifold of R is finite; false, the integers are an infinite closed discrete 0-dimensional embedded submanifold. The counterexample survives via the corrected argument (R\Z contained in the irrationals would force the closed Z to contain Q and hence equal R). (b) The row finite_codimension_complement->residual_comeager asserts that a non-closed immersed Z makes the transfer fail; false for the comeager target, because a second-countable finite-codim immersed submanifold is locally a graph, hence meager, so its complement is comeager (the same error appears in that row's falsifier: the complement of a dense immersed line in the torus is comeager, not 'neither open-dense nor comeager'). Closedness is load-bearing only for the open_dense target. Minor extras, not errors in any verdict: the 'repair' remarks in rows 1 and 4 describe hypotheses that do not in fact repair the failures (for every Borel probability mu on [0,1] there is a comeager set with no mu-full-measure subset, and a meager mu-full-measure set); the strength block's incomparable list omits RC->ODE and ODE->FCC, which are precisely the converses of listed strict pairs and are already covered by the 'converse fails' clause; and, outside the requested scope, the proposed_vocabulary_extension's second 3-point falsifier does not work as stated because {a,b} IS comeager in that B (its complement {c} is nowhere dense), though it is not B-open -- a correct witness for that pair is A=discrete, B=Euclidean, G=Q in [0,1].
